findings.title: Enemies is always empty for a factionless caster (manhunters, wild animals), so area and enemy-list workers never fire for them
findings.detail: AbilityAIContext.Enemies builds from attackTargetsCache.GetPotentialTargetsFor(pawn). For a caster with no faction, that only returns pawns that are themselves in an aggressive mental state and factionless humanlikes; the faction-hostile branch is skipped. So a manhunting wild animal sees no colonists in Enemies even though the Animals setting covers it. InCombat still turns true through EnemyTarget, but any worker that scans ctx.Enemies (NearestEnemy, AimedAtCount, area hostile picks) finds nothing. In the Enemies getter, when pawn.Faction == null, also add the spawned pawns that pawn.HostileTo (or at least EnemyTarget when it is a Pawn).

findings.title: AoEFriendly targeted path gives up after the single best ally fails validation
findings.detail: TryFindTarget keeps only `best` and returns false when PawnOrCell(ability, best) is invalid (e.g. no line of sight). A second-best ally that would pass is never tried. AbilityAIWorker_AoEHostile in the same file collects ranked candidates and tries up to MaxTries=5. Collect the qualifying allies, sort by count, and try a few before returning false.

findings.title: The resume copy of AttackStatic is queued before vanilla has accepted the cast job
findings.detail: TryGiveJob calls EnqueueFirst(resume) and then returns the cast job. Vanilla can still turn it down before starting it (the StartJob guards, or the drop/ReturnToPool branch at Pawn_JobTracker.cs:142-152). In that case the original AttackStatic keeps running with a duplicate queued behind it, so the attack runs again once it ends. Rare and harmless. Queuing the copy from a Notify on the real start (or checking it on the next evaluation) would close the gap. This is my opinion of the risk; the cited lines only show the branch exists.

findings.title: WouldAffect's mech exclusion and psychic sensitivity check copy vanilla on purpose
findings.detail: The Faction.OfMechanoids test matches Psycast.CanApplyPsycastTo exactly, so non-mechanoid-faction mechs are treated the same as in vanilla. The only difference is the 250-tick cached PsychicSensitivity read, so a pawn whose sensitivity just changed can be misjudged for up to about 4 s. Vanilla still validates when the cast happens, so nothing breaks.

findings.title: Wallraise pawn guard is needed because vanilla Valid does not check pawns
findings.detail: CompAbilityEffect_Wallraise.Valid checks Filled/Standable/indestructible things but not pawns. PawnInPattern places the pattern the same way AffectedCells does (target.Cell + (x,0,z), no rotation), so the guard is correct and is the only thing stopping a wall raised onto a pawn.

findings.title: TargetHostile approach only validates the pawn, not its cell
findings.detail: AbilityAIWorker_TargetHostile.TryFindApproachTarget checks ValidIgnoringRange on the enemy pawn only, while the area worker's approach (AbilityAIWorkers.cs:265) also tries p.Position. TryFindTarget here is also pawn-only (FirstValid), so the two are consistent, but a cell-only hostile ability assigned this worker would never approach or cast. If that case is wanted, add the same `|| ValidIgnoringRange(ability, p.Position)` fallback at line 88 and use PawnOrCell in TryFindTarget.

findings.title: Firefighting ignores a burning caster
findings.detail: The burning-ally pass skips allies[i] == ctx.pawn, so a caster on fire never Waterskips itself. That may be intended (a standing pawn pats itself out), but the worker's summary doesn't say so. This is an opinion; the corpus is silent.

findings.title: One missing psycast def aborts every later Royalty rule
findings.detail: All 14 PatchOperationAddModExtension ops sit in one PatchOperationSequence (Patches/AbilityAI_Royalty.xml:13). Vanilla's sequence returns false at the first op that fails, so if another mod removes or renames any one of these AbilityDefs, the game logs a patch failure and none of the later rules are applied. I found no mod on this machine that removes them, so it isn't a current problem. If you want to guard against it, you could wrap each entry in its own PatchOperationConditional, or list them under <Patch> directly inside the FindMod. Either way a missing def costs only its own rule.

findings.title: Psycast names checked against 1.6 only
findings.detail: All 15 targeted defNames exist in the indexed Royalty Abilities.xml (game version 1.6). The mod also loads this root Patches folder for 1.7, and that version isn't in the index. Any name that differs in 1.7 would trigger the sequence failure described above.
